key_insight: Convolution quadrature converts transient acoustic wave propagation in heterogeneous, unbounded media into independent complex-frequency Helmholtz problems that can be solved in parallel.
engineering_relevance: The method supports wave simulations with variable or discontinuous wave speeds while accounting for the unbounded exterior without artificial truncation.
method: Apply A-stable multistep convolution quadrature to solve all time steps through parallel frequency-domain problems.
Couple interior FEM with exterior BEM using overlapping, mutually nonconforming discretizations.
Retain BEM corrections for weakly damped frequencies and omit them where exponential decay makes them negligible.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments confirm predicted temporal and spatial convergence rates and explore multigrid solvers for the interior FEM problems.
watch_item: Choosing when to omit BEM corrections requires care, because small exterior corrections remain relevant at weakly damped frequencies.
paper_title: An all-steps-at-once algorithm for time-domain wave propagation in heterogeneous and unbounded media
